summary.headline: Cemindia Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR2,749 crore, with order book at a record INR32,715 crore and EBITDA margin at 10.2%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total operating income was INR2,749 crore (+25% YoY) and EBITDA INR280 crore (+15% YoY), with EBITDA margin easing to 10.2% from 11.1%. PAT rose 21% YoY to INR131 crore. H1 operating income was INR5,470 crore (+15%) and PAT INR271 crore (+10.8%). Management said Q2 revenue was roughly flat on Q1, unusual for a seasonally weaker quarter, and that a INR1,400 crore QIP and three rating upgrades (ICRA AA, CARE AA-, CRISIL AA, all Stable) were completed. Order book reached INR32,715 crore after INR5,968 crore of wins since quarter start.

financial_highlights.value: INR2,619 crore / INR773 crore; net debt-to-equity ~0.3x

segments.name: Data centres
segments.commentary: Work in hand about INR5,000-6,000 crore; six projects underway (two at Vizag, four in Mumbai) plus new starts in Gujarat. Civil is about 20% of value and MEP about 80%; large revenue expected from mid-January 2027.

segments.name: Marine / ports
segments.commentary: Dhamra Port (INR800 crore) and Project Varsha for Indian Navy outer harbour (INR700 crore) won in Q2. Jatadhari Port marine job nearing completion. Vadhavan Port work restarted; port order book about INR1,500 crore.

segments.name: Metro / urban infra
segments.commentary: Q2 and October wins include Jaipur Metro (INR781 crore) and K-RIDE Bengaluru (INR660 crore). Pune and Delhi Metro work started; CMRL and Bengaluru Metro jobs nearing completion.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of 20-25% maintained for FY27.
EBITDA margin guided at around 10% or more on average through the year; management did not confirm the 10.5% full-year figure asked about.
Order inflow target of INR25,000 crore for FY27 reiterated; management said it will be achieved and could be exceeded.
Management said H2 revenue and margin gains from current work in hand will mainly come in FY28, with little expected in FY27.
Management expects at least 25% CAGR in top line over the next three years.
Capex of about INR150 crore in H1 FY27; INR150-200 crore more in H2 and FY27; large TBM-led capex of INR1,000-1,500 crore expected in FY28 if a large-diameter tunnel job is won.
capex_capacity: Capex to date is about INR150 crore (H1 FY27); management expects a similar amount in the remainder of FY27.
A large-diameter TBM job, such as Bengaluru, could add INR1,000-1,500 crore of capex, with deployment over 14-16 months and the main spend in FY28.
INR1,400 crore QIP (1.26 crore shares at INR1,108) was oversubscribed 2.3x; proceeds go to capex, debt repayment, working capital and general corporate purposes.
Management cites four other large TBM tenders in pipeline. TBMs could be sourced outside China if needed.
Working capital is 96 days and inventory 28 days.
demand_pricing: Order book INR32,715 crore, an all-time high; includes INR5,968 crore of wins since quarter start (INR3,487 crore in Q2, INR2,481 crore in October).
Order book mix: group about 53-54%; group-sourced inflows were roughly 70%+ in recent quarters.
Revenue mix H1 FY27: about 35-36% from group entities, balance non-group.
Eight business areas; maritime, urban infra, MRTS and airports, and industrial structures and buildings together make up 62% of order book; data centres about 15%.
External pipeline cited at about INR1.3 lakh crore; group-related pipeline about INR50,000 crore (group capex about INR2 lakh crore per year).
Margin range across segments 8-13%; data centres not expected above 10%; underground and marine carry higher margins.
Navi Mumbai Phase 2 (Adani) in advanced discussions; contract award expected Q3 or Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins trend in H2, and can full-year margin reach 10.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated margin of around 10% plus on average through the year. Some new jobs (Vadhavan, Morsagar, Munger, K-RIDE, DMRC, Pune) have not yet crossed the margin-recognition threshold and should convert in one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 order inflow details and October wins?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 wins: data centre from group (about INR1,000 crore, Andhra Pradesh), Dhamra Port INR800 crore, Project Varsha (Navy) INR700 crore, JSW INR235 crore. October: Jaipur Metro INR781 crore, K-RIDE INR660 crore, Assam job from group (INR1,000+ crore).

qa_highlights.question: Is revenue guidance of 20-25% still valid, and what is capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, 20-25% revenue growth is maintained. H1 capex about INR150 crore, with INR150-200 crore more in the rest of the year. Major TBM capex of INR1,000-1,500 crore expected in FY28 if a large job is won.

qa_highlights.question: Data centre execution timelines and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: First data centre erection expected from January-February 2027, with large revenue from mid-January. Civil takes about 24 months, then MEP. Margins expected at 10% or below.

qa_highlights.question: Is Adani/group tunnel project and China TBM restriction an issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot comment on group awards. If the group awards the job, Cemindia is highly likely to get it. TBM sourcing is not a constraint; other countries are being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: ROE pressure from capex and dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said short-term ROE may fall, with scale-up after about 24 months as large machines are deployed. The INR5,000 crore approval is only enabling; leverage will be used prudently.

qa_highlights.question: Vadhavan Port revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give revenue guidance for Vadhavan Port, saying work has restarted but pace is still to be seen. Port order book is about INR1,500 crore.

risks_watch: Margin pressure: Q2 EBITDA margin fell YoY to 10.2%, and management flagged certification delays and jobs not yet at margin-recognition threshold.
Dependence on group: about 53-54% of order book and about 35-36% of H1 revenue from group entities; large TBM capex hinges on group tunnel award.
ROE dilution risk as capex-heavy growth comes before revenue; management expects scale-up only after about 24 months.
Vadhavan Port execution pace and revenue timing still unclear.
Data centre revenue ramp depends on MEP deliveries from January 2027; margins expected at or below 10%.
Navi Mumbai Phase 2 award timing (Q3-Q4 FY27) and October-November order flow vs INR25,000 crore inflow target.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book, ratings and the INR25,000 crore inflow target, but cautious on margin (around 10% average) and vague on Vadhavan Port timing and TBM-linked capex. Management deflected questions on group awards and L1 positions, stating they are subject to competitive bidding.
key_quotes: Today, we have INR32,000 crores of work in hand, which is also significant because normally it used to be around INR20,000, INR21,000.
Nitesh Sharma: For future, we say that at least for next three years' time, we definitely look forward for keeping a CAGR of 25% on the top line.
If group gets the job, there is a high possibility that we will get the job. That is for sure.
ROE may fall little bit short term, but definitely it will have major impact going forward in long term.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25% was held, backed by a record INR32,715 crore order book (including INR5,968 crore of wins since quarter start) and a 25% YoY Q2 revenue rise; capex is modest (~INR150 crore in H1 plus INR150-200 crore in H2) with the large TBM-led expansion (INR1,000-1,500 crore) contingent on winning a tender and landing mainly in FY28.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue grew 25% YoY in Q2 and 15% in H1, FY27 revenue growth of 20-25% is held, and record order book of INR32,715 crore with INR5,968 crore of wins since quarter start backs volume.

rows.why: Management cites four other large TBM tenders in pipeline and a possible INR1,000-1,500 crore TBM capex; the INR5,000 crore approval is enabling, though utilisation is not disclosed so the call rests on order-led need rather than a utilisation trigger.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: Navi Mumbai Phase 2 award (Adani)
rows.why: Management said the contract award is expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27 and discussions are advanced, but group award timing is outside its control and not confirmed.

rows.why: Target reiterated and said it will be achieved and could be exceeded, with INR5,968 crore of wins since quarter start against H1 inflows and a INR32,715 crore order book.
